S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it. Other thermal incidents shall be reported within 5 business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident presents a credible safety risk requiring customer action, and promptly provide any subsequent safety instructions.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The maximum allowed failure rate shall be 8% for any model. Manufacturers shall submit per-model test results, including the test date, sample size, and failure rate, to the relevant regulator and provide those results to customers who buy that model.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Newly installed systems shall include remote emergency shut-off capability no later than three years after this standard takes effect. For systems already installed on that date, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent upgrade within six years, where technically feasible, and shall communicate safe interim procedures to owners.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new home battery systems manufactured 36 months or more after this standard is adopted shall include built-in fire suppression designed for the system's battery chemistry and enclosure.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a rolling 12-month period, the manufacturer shall promptly report the rate and supporting data to the relevant regulator and affected customers. The regulator shall promptly assess the risk and may require a recall or other corrective action; the manufacturer shall initiate a recall when that assessment finds the risk unacceptable.

document.section_notes: The 8% permanent test ceiling (S2) replaces the 5% limit and is the main gain for Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%), while per-model results go to purchasers and regulators but not the public, respecting both red lines. The 8-per-100,000 figure in S5 no longer triggers an automatic recall; it triggers mandatory reporting and a regulator-led assessment, with corrective action that can replace recall indefinitely, which largely protects Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9). S1 reporting is strict (24 hours for serious incidents, all incidents covered), and S4 built-in suppression from 36 months is at the edge of the acceptable range.
